source: The sun winks through the pines, scattering beams on the ferns below. Retired couples, active parents, and idle minds wander peacefully along the many trails. They move like monorails, never deviating, making scheduled stops to open their eyelids and peer out at a sequence of views and vistas. Creatures of the pines avoid the monorail of humans, and live hard lives of competition amongst themselves.
target: 阳光在松林间眨眼，将光束洒向下方的蕨类。退休伴侣、爱活动的父母与放空心思的人，沿着交错步道安然漫游。他们像单轨列车，从不偏离路线，按表停靠，睁开眼皮，望向一幕幕景色。松林里的生物避开这列人类列车，在彼此竞争中艰辛求生。

source: LIFE IN PINE HILLS PARK
target: 松丘公园的生命

source: The casual hum of the park often dissipates quickly and gives way to peaceful unpopulated nights. As the sun drops, cool pockets of air settle down between the hills – eventually growing into roving bands of fog that stifle light and sound. To the paranoid, the park is loud; to the calm-hearted, the park is silent. Each night the will of the pines fights back against relentless human expansion. New ferns blossom, earthworms rebuild, and trees sprout buds. Despite all its pain, the forest chooses not to give up.
target: 公园闲散的喧声往往很快消退，让位给宁静无人的夜。日落时，一团团冷空气沉入丘陵之间，渐渐形成游移的雾带，遮蔽光线，也压低声响。多疑者听见公园喧嚣，心安者听见公园寂静。每一夜，松林的意志都反抗着人类无休止的扩张。新蕨舒展，蚯蚓重整土壤，树木萌芽。即使饱受痛苦，森林仍选择不放弃。

source: A DICHOTOMY OF TWO TIMES
target: 两个时刻的并存

source: Upon sight of this horror, the location of Everly Praetis' untimely murder, a dichotomy of two times invades the mind. There is the now. Since the murder, time has elapsed, the blood no longer flows – it has dried, it is earthly and dark. The creatures of the pines have begun to reclaim the site, and the forces of nature too: erosion, sunlight, and wind are already beginning to hide away this scar. But there is also the then. The axe remains stuck in the precise position where it ended a life. From it, one can faintly imagine the positions of the person’s involved. Their footprints show some confusing dance through the fog and into finality. One can see the dark biblical chaos of this moment as if it were still present. Yes, there are two times here, then, and now: each pervasive, each searing, and each relentless in its control of the memory. One cannot forget these two times. One cannot tear them apart.
target: 看见这片惨景，艾芙莉・普雷蒂斯横遭杀害的地方，两个时刻同时闯入脑海。一个是现在。命案之后，时间已经流逝，血不再流动——它干了，变得黯淡，融入尘土。松林生物开始收回这片地方，自然的力量亦然：侵蚀、阳光与风，已开始掩去这道伤疤。但还有当时。斧头仍卡在终结生命时的确切位置。从它的位置，可以隐约想像当事人彼此站在哪里。脚印勾勒出一场令人困惑的舞，穿过雾，走向终局。人仿佛仍能看见那一刻，如圣经灾厄般黑暗的混乱。是的，这里有两个时刻，当时与现在：都无所不在，都灼痛人心，都牢牢掌控记忆。人无法忘记这两个时刻，也无法将它们分开。

source: Several hundred yards away, at the head of the park, piled teddy bears, flowers, and candles make it hard to decipher the park's entrance sign. There, humanity reigns – riddled with grief, but still humanity. Decency has kept secret this spot, the site of the murder. And so here, there is no humanity. There are no sobbing friends, no huddled prayers, no collections taken up for family. Here there is only a shadow – cast by ultimate rage – the remnants of complexity – complexities that may never be known.
target: 几百码外的公园入口，堆满泰迪熊、鲜花与蜡烛，让入口标志几乎难以辨认。那里，人性仍在——满是悲痛，却仍是人性。出于善意，人们没有公开这个地方，命案现场。因此，这里没有人情。没有啜泣的朋友，没有相依祈祷的人群，没有替家属发起的募款。这里只有一道阴影——极致愤怒投下的影子——复杂纠葛的残迹——也许永远无人知晓的纠葛。

source: CAN EVERY COMPLEXITY BE DISCOVERED?
target: 所有纠葛都能被解开吗？

source: TRASH HAVEN
target: 垃圾乐园

source: It seems all the older students at Asbury High know about the small path, as indiscernible as a game trail, that leads deep into Pine Hills Park and ends at a patch of trampled grass. “The Clearing” – a plot for anarchy. Shooting empty beer cans after church, smashing bottles against trees for the thrill of the shatter, smoking weed under the stars in peace, spray painting dicks and jokes on fallen logs, summoning ouija board ghosts, tugging each other’s clothes off, and celebrating the end of the school year with a bonfire of homework notebooks. How old is this trash haven? No one can say. Though somehow it always stays familiar.
target: 阿斯伯里高中的高年级学生，似乎都知道那条像兽径般难以辨识的小路。它深入松丘公园，止于一片踩平的草地。「空地」——一块无法无天之地。做完礼拜后朝空啤酒罐射击，为了碎裂的快感把酒瓶砸向树干，在星空下安静抽大麻，在倒木上喷画鸡巴与笑话，用通灵板召鬼，扯下彼此衣服，还有把作业本堆成营火，庆祝学年结束。这座垃圾乐园有多久历史？没人说得准。却不知为何，总是那么熟悉。

source:
An abandoned grave is nothing at first. A cracked slab of stone covered in vines, moss, and bird shit. But it slowly seduces the visitor. First with its presence – why here? Then with its heft – who did this? With its words and dates – who was Sadie Sloane, how did she die young? 

Curiosity grows into imagination. A precocious child in the woods, perhaps lost, perhaps taken, perhaps devoured. No. She fell from a branch here, her secret playground. Father told her not to clamber around like a monkey, so she did it out of sight. 

Imagination grows so big that it spreads itself like memory. Like  of someone we know, or at least feel like we do. It all must mean something.  Unexpectedly we are somber, standing before a cracked slab of stone covered in vines, moss, and bird shit.
target:
一座荒废坟墓，起初什么也不是。只是块裂开的石板，覆满藤蔓、苔藓与鸟屎。但它慢慢引诱访客。先是它的存在——为什么在这里？再来是它的分量——谁立的？接着是字句与日期——莎蒂・斯隆是谁，怎么会年纪轻轻就死了？

好奇长成想像。一个早慧的孩子走进树林，也许迷路，也许被掳走，也许遭野兽吞食。不。她是在这里从树枝跌落，这是她秘密的游乐场。父亲不准她像猴子那样爬来爬去，所以她躲起来爬。

想像膨胀得如此巨大，像记忆般蔓延。像是关于某个我们认识的人，至少感觉认识的人。这一切，必定有什么意义。不知不觉，我们神情肃穆，站在那块覆满藤蔓、苔藓与鸟屎的裂石前。

source: OFFERINGS OF THE DEAD
target: 死者的赠礼

source: Insects make up 90 percent of all life forms on earth. Their realm is more vast, deep, and intricate than we can fathom, with histories and empires ten-thousand times greater than our own. They arrived centuries ago, brought by the delicious allure of daisy fields. Small and driven, this is where they toil.
target: 昆虫占地球所有生命形态的九成。牠们的领域，比我们所能理解的更广阔、更深邃、更错综复杂，其历史与帝国比我们的庞大万倍。几百年前，雏菊花田的美味诱惑将牠们带到这里。身形微小，意志坚定，这就是牠们辛勤劳作之地。

source: UNFATHOMABLE EMPIRES
target: 深不可测的帝国

source: WHEAT AND WILL
target: 麦田与意志

source:
The beauty and romance of a wheat field masks its past. 

Sturdy trees were felled, thinned and hauled. Embedded stones were  carved from rest and lugged to form a long stone wall. The stubborn earth was then split by the wedge of a heavy plow, breaking dirt into rows so long they met the horizon. Calloused hands, aching backs, swollen feet – a wheat field is an act of sheer will onto the land. 

Where does such will get its strength?  

A vision for the future.
target:
麦田的美丽与浪漫，掩盖了它的过去。

粗壮的树木遭砍倒、疏伐、拖走。深埋的石块被撬离安眠处，搬去砌成长长石墙。接着，沉重犁刃剖开顽固的大地，将土翻成一列列垄沟，长得直抵天际。长茧的手、酸痛的背、肿胀的脚——麦田，是纯粹意志施加于土地的结果。

这份意志，从哪里得到力量？

对未来的愿景。

source: VIVA LA HALLUCINATION
target: 幻觉万岁

source:
Violent riots spread across France preceding the French Revolution. The upheaval, lasting from July 22 to August 6 in 1789, was known as “The Great Fear” and was sparked by poor grain harvests that year. Peasants, afraid that the remaining grain would be hoarded by the wealthy or stolen by brigands, were frenzied into a mass panic and took to looting the lands and manors of the nobility. 

Due to the low-yield harvest, all grain was kept that year. Even the grain contaminated with ergot fungus – a growth that contains psychoactive alkaloids.  

With little option for other food, peasants looted and ate the contaminated grain. An ergot epidemic swept through France.

It has been considered that this mass hallucinogenic hysteria paved a step towards the all-out revolution that reshaped French society.
target:
法国大革命前夕，暴动席卷法国。这场从 1789 年 7 月 22 日持续至 8 月 6 日的动荡，被称为「大恐慌」，起因是当年谷物歉收。农民害怕剩余谷物遭富人囤积，或被盗匪偷走，陷入集体恐慌，开始洗劫贵族的土地与庄园。

由于收成不足，当年所有谷物都被保留下来。即使是遭麦角菌污染的谷物——这种真菌含有影响精神的生物碱——也不例外。

缺乏其他食物选择，农民抢夺并吃下受污染谷物。麦角中毒蔓延法国。

有一种看法认为，这场集体致幻狂乱，为后来重塑法国社会的全面革命，铺下了一步。

source: GATEWAY
target: 通道

source: Pioneered by French fur trappers in the 1700s, trampled into a worn dirt road by settlers heading West, and paved in the 1930s to bring jobs back to the Depression-damaged town. Route 25 has always been a road for conquest and opportunity of all shades — from the good to the criminal, and the gray area inbetween.
target: 十八世纪，法国皮草猎人开出这条路；西进的移民将它踩成磨损的土路；到了 1930 年代，人们将它铺平，为受大萧条重创的城镇带回工作。二十五号公路，始终是各式征服与机遇的道路——从善事到犯罪，以及两者之间的灰色地带。

source: ADOPTION
target: 认养

source:
For 43 years, the Asbury Birdwatchers Club have adopted the first two miles of Route 25 that leave Asbury heading  West. A local record. 

Twice a year they take to the roadsides with neon vests and trash-picker sticks, as habitually as geese migrating in fall and late spring. To the passersby that honk in encouragement, they wave and smile and some flap their arms in jest. 

No one questions them. No one asks the Club members why they volunteer so diligently. It’s happily assumed they are all pitching in to make the world a little nicer. 

The most enthusiastic birdwatchers have a secret: clean roads mean more roadkill. More roadkill means more predatory flyers. 

Beautiful red-tailed hawks, golden eagles, great horned owls, merlin falcons and little American kestrel.
target:
四十三年来，阿斯伯里赏鸟俱乐部认养了二十五号公路离镇西行的前两英里路段，创下本地纪录。

一年两次，他们穿上萤光背心、拿起捡垃圾的夹子，走到路旁，规律得像秋季与晚春迁徙的雁群。路人鸣喇叭鼓励时，他们微笑挥手，有些还开玩笑地拍动双臂。

没有人质疑。没有人问俱乐部成员，为什么如此勤奋地当志工。大家欣然认定，他们只是齐心协力，让世界美好一点。

最热心的赏鸟者藏着一个秘密：干净的道路，意味着更多路杀动物。更多路杀动物，意味着更多猛禽。

美丽的红尾𫛭、金雕、大角鸮、灰背隼，还有小小的美洲隼。

source: LAYERS OF LIFE
target: 生命的地层

source: The strata in the earth reveals settlements of the past pressed into the soil. The deeper the dig, the deeper the history. Farm animal bones and feed seeds – a ranch from the mid-1800s. Further down, chunks of wood with daub and a charcoal deposit – a log home and hearth from the late 1600s. Below that, ornate bone beads, wood bowls and flint arrowheads – an asi, a common Cherokee winter home from 900. Deeper yet, beyond assumptions of the possible, ancient pottery shards and crude plow tools emerge. Layers and layers of lives before our own are preserved for discovery, for understanding. Waiting for us to consider our past selves. We, who are high up on the surface, busy and distracted.
target: 地层揭露了被压进土里的昔日聚落。挖得愈深，历史愈深。家畜骨骸与饲料种子——十九世纪中叶的牧场。再往下，是沾着泥灰的木块与木炭堆积——十七世纪末的木屋与炉灶。更下方，是精致骨珠、木碗与燧石箭头——一间asi，西元九百年常见的切罗基冬季住屋。再深一点，超越我们对可能性的想像，古老陶片与粗糙犁具浮现了。一层又一层，早于我们的生命被保存下来，等待发现，等待理解。等着我们思索过去的自己。而我们高高地活在地表，忙碌，分心。

source: STUBBORN MAGNIFICENCE
target: 固执的宏伟

source: Bricks and bricks and bricks and bricks of sun-baked clay, carefully organized in pattern and line. An ancient plaza spreading in all directions, sealing the soil and the deep groundwaters beneath it. A lid laid block by block across years and years. Such grand designs are rarely driven by pragmatism. Magnificence needs stubbornness. Magnificence needs many hands that work in tandem, unified in hubris and will and the obstinate belief that their work can defy their impermanence.
target: 一块又一块、一块又一块日晒泥砖，仔细依照图样与线条排列。古老广场向四面伸展，封住下方土壤与深层地下水。年复一年，一砖一砖盖上的盖子。如此宏大的设计，很少出于实用考量。宏伟需要固执。宏伟需要许多双手同心工作，以傲慢、意志，以及那份顽固的信念凝聚起来：相信他们的作品，能抵抗自身的短暂。

source: Archaeologists debate with their colleagues about how to leave a dig site. Fill it and return at a later time, or cover it up to preserve the work, or open it for public viewing – all options share costs and benefits to the health of the site. Another vocal group, the town developers, barge into the conversation. Town council and public politicians soon follow. In no time, many loud voices are talking over each other, spitting reasons and needs and goals. But the one voice that may matter most is never heard. The voice of the people from the past, who had an intention for their lives and their eternal rest.
target: 考古学家与同僚争论，该如何离开挖掘现场。回填，以后再来？覆盖起来，保存成果？还是开放公众参观？每种选择，对遗址的保存都有利弊。另一群大嗓门——镇上的开发商——闯进讨论。镇议会与政界人士很快跟进。转眼间，众人争相高声说话，吐出各自的理由、需求与目标。但那个或许最重要的声音，始终没被听见。那是过去之人的声音，他们对自己的生命，以及永恒安息，曾有过期望。

source: THE UNHEARD
target: 未被听见的声音

source: Daisy Pond is an artificial creation. Man made. Carved, filled shallow and bordered with daisies by the nephew of an old Puritan who established the first European settlement in the area – Bancroft. Sitting between shrublands teeming with snails and wild fowl and swaths of shade-drenched pine forest, a bronze plaque welcomes visitors with a curious statement: “You were always meant to be here.”
target: 雏菊池是人造的。出自人手。建立本地第一个欧洲聚落——班克罗夫特——的那位老清教徒，他的姪子挖出池塘，注入浅水，在池边种满雏菊。池塘坐落于蜗牛与野禽繁盛的灌木地，以及大片阴影笼罩的松林之间。一块铜牌以奇妙的话语迎接访客：「你一直都注定会来这里。」

source: POND PREDESIGNED
target: 预先设计的池塘
